title: 14.6 A 28nm 64kb Bit-Rotated Hybrid-CIM Macro with an Embedded Sign-Bit-Processing Array and a Multi-Bit-Fusion Dual-Granularity Cooperative Quantizer
problem: Hybrid compute-in-memory (HCIM) designs face three key challenges: (1) optimally defining the digital-analog boundary without sacrificing accuracy or overhead, (2) handling sign-bit processing overhead in bit-rotated schemes, and (3) wasting energy on low-accuracy-contributed low-bit quantization in analog portions.
motivation: Hybrid CIM combines digital precision with analog efficiency for inference workloads; addressing these three challenges enables better accuracy-area-power tradeoffs than pure digital or analog approaches.
method: The design uses a 64 kilobyte hybrid compute-in-memory block (hardware that stores and processes data in the same place) that feeds input features one bit at a time in a rotating pattern (bit-rotated). It processes the sign bit (the +/−) right at the first multiply-and-add step, avoiding the accuracy loss that occurs when other approaches handle signs separately—whether processing all bits at once or one at a time. An embedded sign-bit-processing array efficiently handles compression between positive and negative numbers. A multi-bit-fusion dual-granularity cooperative quantizer then dynamically allocates precision between fast analog hardware and precise digital hardware, based on each bit's significance (how much it contributes to accuracy).
key_novelty: The core innovation is integrating sign-bit processing into the first computation step and using bit-significance to dynamically balance precision between analog and digital, eliminating wasted energy on low-significance bits.
contributions: Bit-rotated feature-in scheme with first-stage sign-bit handling, avoiding error pollution
Embedded sign-bit-processing array reducing digital overhead vs. separate solutions
Multi-bit-fusion cooperative quantizer with dynamic precision allocation
28 nm implementation achieving balanced accuracy-energy-area for inference
baselines: prior bit-parallel HCIM with accuracy loss
prior bit-serial HCIM with error pollution
limitations: Specific energy, throughput, and accuracy metrics (e.g., inference accuracy on benchmarks) not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Hybrid CIM with sign-bit processing and cooperative quantization for efficient neural inference
